checks.1_zhinx_equals_gap9: I assembled every RV32 Zhinx instruction LLVM defines (30 forms: fadd/fsub/fmul/fdiv/fsqrt.h with static and dynamic rm, fmadd/fmsub/fnmadd/fnmsub.h, fsgnj/fsgnjn/fsgnjx.h, fmin/fmax.h, feq/flt/fle.h, fclass.h, fcvt.w/wu.h, fcvt.h.w/wu, fcvt.s.h, fcvt.h.s, fneg/fabs aliases) with llvm-mc -mattr=+zfinx,+zhinx and with GAP9 GNU as -march=rv32imcxgap9: 30/30 byte-identical (logs/20-F035-review/zhinx_all.s, mc.enc, gas.dis). GVSoC2's Xf16 subset (gvsoc2/core/models/cpu/iss/isa_gen/isa_smallfloats.py:21-72), which Ri5ky (GAP9 FC and cluster) always includes, implements every one of these. The Zhinx instructions GAP9 lacks are fcvt.h.d/fcvt.d.h (GVSoC has them commented out) and the RV64 fcvt.l*/h.l* forms. llvm-mc -mattr=+xgap rejects all of them, because they need Zdinx or RV64 and xgap9 implies neither. fround.h, fli.h and fminm.h are Zfa, which conflicts with Zfinx, and are rejected. Upstream sign-extends Zhinx GPR results explicitly (RISCVISelLowering.cpp:15132, 'Don't do this with Zhinx'), so GVSoC writing results zero-extended does not break any known-bits assumption. Enabling Zhinx therefore cannot make clang emit an fp16 instruction GAP9 does not implement.
checks.2_names_and_implications: -march parses: rv32imc_xgap9 now defines __riscv_zhinx, __riscv_zhinxmin, __riscv_xpulpf16alt, __riscv_xpulpfvec (all 1000000) in addition to what it defined before. A -dM diff against build/int-20 shows only these 4 macros plus the version string. No __riscv_xf* macro is defined. rv32imc_xpulpf16alt gives zfinx. rv32imc_xpulpfvec gives xpulpv 2.0 + zfinx. xpulpf16alt1p0 and xpulpfvec1 are accepted, xpulpf16alt2 is rejected (unsupported version), and rv32imfc_xpulpfvec is rejected (f/zfinx). The ELF attribute is rv32i2p1_m2p0_c2p0_zicsr2p0_zmmul1p0_zfinx1p0_zhinx1p0_zhinxmin1p0_xgap9p0_xpulpf16alt1p0_xpulpfvec1p0_xpulpv2p0, and llc -mattr=+xgap prints the same set. The Snitch extensions (FeatureExtXf* in RISCVInstrInfoXsmallfloatGen.td, names xfalthalf/xfvechalf/xfvecalthalf/..., version 0.1) have different names, imply nothing, and are implied by nothing new. Every Snitch smallfloat and Xfrep instruction is under a Predicates list containing only its own HasExtXf*, so xgap9 enables none of them. The implications match design 6.3 (xpulpfvec implies xpulpv2; its .h/.ah halves are to be predicated on zhinx/xpulpf16alt in T2), plus zfinx, which is justified by vfcpka.h.s.

checks.4_numerical_equivalence: I rebuilt build/20-F035 from the committed head 441ded47bcd4 (incremental, clang llc llvm-mc lld TargetParserTests...). (a) Reran the worker's run.sh (f16tiny.c + design numeq.c, GAP9 GCC -DT=float16 -march=rv32imcxgap9 -mPE=8 -mFC=1 -O2 vs clang -DT=_Float16 -march=rv32imc_xgap9 -ffp-contract=fast -O2) on ri5ky_testbench: f16tiny IDENTICAL 16/16 and numeq IDENTICAL 12/12, and the GCC output equals the worker's log. (b) My own probe, logs/20-F035-review/rv.c, prints every result value, not hashes. 160 inputs: 24 specials (+-0, +-1, +-inf, qNaN 0x7e00, sNaN 0x7c01, negative/payload NaNs 0xfe55/0x7d23, min/max subnormal, min normal, max finite, 1-ulp neighbours), 40 subnormal-heavy, 16 overflow-prone, 80 random bit patterns. Operations: add, sub, mul, div, contracted fma/fms/fnmadd/fnmsub, sqrt, from int, from unsigned and from float, each under frm = RNE, RTZ, RDN and RUP (set with csrw frm), plus min, max, lt, le, eq, to float and to int. The GCC and clang outputs are byte-identical over all 8800 values. Instruction mix: both use fadd/fsub/fmul/fdiv/fsqrt/fmadd/fmsub/fnmadd/fnmsub/fmin/fmax/flt/fle/feq.h and the fcvt.* forms, with no libcalls. (c) I checked those GVSoC results against an independent exact-rational IEEE-754/RISC-V reference (logs/20-F035-review/ref.py, ref-clang.out). Every RNE result matches: subnormals, signed zeros, canonical NaN 0x7e00 for every NaN result (no payload or sign propagation, as the RISC-V spec requires), min/max minimumNumber semantics with -0<+0, and compares. The only mismatches (681/8800) are in directed modes: an overflowing result gives inf where IEEE wants max-finite (RTZ, and RDN/RUP toward zero), and one case where a tiny RDN product gives -0 instead of -min-subnormal. These are GVSoC flexfloat properties. They are identical for GCC and clang, so they do not affect the compiler claim. GVSoC aborts on RMM ('Unimplemented rounding mode'), so RMM cannot be tested on this simulator.

observations_not_blocking: GVSoC deviates from IEEE on directed-rounding overflow (returns inf instead of max-finite) and on at least one directed-rounding underflow, and aborts on RMM. This affects GCC and clang equally, but anyone using GVSoC as an fp16 oracle in non-RNE modes should know about it.

clang lowers __builtin_sqrtf16 to a call to sqrtf16 unless -fno-math-errno is given, and GAP9 has no such libm routine (link error). GCC's __builtin_pulp_f16sqrt emits fsqrt.h. This is clang's existing errno behaviour, not F035. It is relevant to the SDK clang flags and fp16 T4 (FloatDefines.h maps f16 sqrt to the pulp builtin).

-march=rv32imc_xgap9_zdinx (explicitly adding D-in-GPR, which GAP9 lacks) would enable fcvt.h.d/fcvt.d.h. -march=rv32imc_xgap9_xfalthalf (explicitly adding Snitch extensions) is accepted. Both are user-requested combinations, not something xgap9 implies, and neither existed only because of this change.
Design T0's f16 post-increment load (setIndexedLoadAction POST_INC f16) is not done. The worker lists it under other_errors_seen (codegen-core cluster, performance only).
